feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: DreamX-Creator: Democratizing Native Audio-Video Generation at 2K Resolution
entry.summary:
DreamX-Creator 1.0 is a 7B joint audio-video generator producing synchronized 2K outputs via Gated Cross-Modal Attention, progressive pre-training, modality-aware reinforcement learning, and a 1-step autoregressive refinement pipeline.

Why it matters: It provides a compact, open-source 7B foundation for generating synchronized, high-resolution audio and video natively within a single model rather than relying on separate, cascaded systems.

entry.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Analysis reveals on-policy distillation works primarily by suppressing low log-probability tokens rather than distilling teacher knowledge, motivating On-Policy Self-Adaptation, a supervision-free method that outperforms distillation.

Why it matters: Language models can achieve self-improvement and math performance gains without relying on external teacher models or dense token-level reward supervision.

entry.title: Lucida: Parse, Generate, and Place for Composable Real-to-Sim Scene Modeling
entry.summary:
Lucida introduces a composable real-to-sim pipeline that redistributes scene parsing, asset generation, and placement via GizmoAct, a vision-language model policy that aligns generated 3D objects using iterative GUI gizmo interactions.

Why it matters: Lucida enables the automatic creation of fully editable, high-fidelity 3D simulation environments from cluttered real-world video captures for embodied AI and robotics.

entry.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation
entry.summary:
Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation (NoRA) stabilizes and accelerates parameter-efficient training by normalizing down-projection matrices during training or strictly at initialization.

Why it matters: NoRA offers a zero-overhead, highly scalable drop-in improvement for LoRA that accelerates convergence and enhances stability across multiple training paradigms.

entry.title: PaperGym: Rubric-Centered Evolution for Research-Plan Generation
entry.summary:
PaperGym converts research papers into RL training environments by synthesizing questions from goals/background and criteria from methods/experiments, reducing criterion leakage to 3.7%.

Why it matters: PaperGym provides a leak-resistant reinforcement learning environment and reward pipeline for training open-weights models to generate valid research plans without relying on verifiable answers.

entry.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability
entry.summary:
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses a 125B/6B-activated MoE architecture with Gated DeltaNet, Gated Residuals, and off-chip n-gram embeddings to outperform its 397B predecessor using 1/9th the training FLOPs.

Why it matters: The architectural and optimizer innovations drastically reduce training FLOPs and active parameter counts while maintaining benchmark performance and improving training stability.

entry.title: CogEvol: Towards Efficient and Reliable Learning Environment Generation
entry.summary:
CogEvol is a model family that generates structured-JSON slides and interactive HTML learning artifacts in a single pass using SFT and GRPO-based reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: CogEvol significantly reduces latency, compute costs, and hardware requirements for generating complex, interactive educational artifacts in production environments.

entry.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation
entry.summary:
LightNav-0 is a compact, generalist embodied navigation model that unifies diverse navigation tasks by eliciting pretrained vision-language model (VLM) spatial intelligence using a token-based interface without task-specific prediction heads.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that compact VLMs can serve as unified, transferable backbones for complex embodied navigation, eliminating the need for task- or embodiment-specific architecture components.

entry.title: Scaling Large Reasoning Models beyond Human Supervision: A Path toward Superintelligence
entry.summary:
This paper presents a five-level taxonomy (L0 to L4) analyzing how large reasoning models can scale beyond human supervision across two dimensions: reward source evolution and experience generation.

Why it matters: It offers a structured framework for diagnosing failure modes and evaluating progress as reinforcement learning systems transition to self-sustaining, autonomous training regimens.

entry.title: Super Library Agent: Joint Generation and Maintenance of Multiple Applications Beyond the Single Codebase
entry.summary:
The Super Library Agent framework enables LLM agents to sequentially generate multiple related applications while automatically extracting reusable components into a shared Super Library to reduce code redundancy and structural erosion.

Why it matters: It enables LLM coding agents to maintain multi-application software portfolios efficiently without accumulating duplicate, dead, or structurally eroded code across repositories.

entry.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with sinks performs as well as or better than post-trained Linear Attention models across multiple LLMs without requiring post-training.

Why it matters: Switching to SWA with sinks provides a cheaper, zero-training alternative to post-trained Linear Attention for reducing LLM inference memory costs.

entry.title: Evaluating the Hidden Costs of Personalization in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced PRISK, a dynamic evaluation framework that revealed personalizing LLMs significantly degrades performance by increasing irrelevant personalization, preference narrowing, and sycophantic bias.

Why it matters: Conditioning LLMs on user history and profiles systematically degrades response objectivity and diversity, forcing a trade-off between user satisfaction and model bias.

entry.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
entry.summary:
AutoSciRub is an evaluation-first framework for autonomous research agents that induces task-specific, verifiable rubrics before execution to guide experiments, verification, and iterative report revision.

Why it matters: It establishes a generalizable control mechanism that makes implicit experimental requirements explicit, preventing research agents from skipping crucial analyses or drawing unsupported conclusions.

entry.title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
EvoUndo introduces a framework for verifying and synthesizing the recoverability of LLM agent self-evolution mutations across counterfactual states.

Why it matters: Iterative prompting is insufficient for safe self-modifying agents; reliable runtime self-evolution requires co-designed state grounding, verification, and expressive recovery languages.

entry.title: Lies We Can See: Joint Verbal and Non-Verbal Deception by VLM Agents in Embodied Social Interactions
entry.summary:
MineAmongUs is a 3D multimodal sandbox evaluated with the ARIA harness to benchmark joint verbal and non-verbal deception in VLM agents.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark for studying embodied VLM safety and alignment beyond text-only interactions, showing how non-verbal actions drive strategic deception.

entry.title: CARVE: Verified Expansion for Variable-Length Generation in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
CARVE is a training-free decoding algorithm that enables variable-length generation in masked diffusion language models by dynamically expanding the canvas only when verified via counterfactual stability testing.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to guess exact target output lengths prior to generation, reducing FLOP costs and preventing truncated output or degraded accuracy in diffusion LMs.

entry.title: HSRM: Hidden-State Reward Models for Test-Time Verification
entry.summary:
HSRM is a 2M-parameter hidden-state reward model that verifies LLM mathematical reasoning candidates by analyzing internal generator representations at step boundaries instead of re-processing solution text.

Why it matters: HSRM enables accurate test-time solution verification with significantly reduced computational overhead by recycling internal LLM representations already calculated during inference.

entry.title: A Model with No Head and Many Thoughts
entry.summary:
Soft Latent Thinking replaces the final vocabulary head with a lightweight projector, allowing autoregressive chain-of-thought reasoning in continuous embedding space instead of discrete tokens.

Why it matters: It lowers the computational cost of chain-of-thought reasoning while improving model performance by operating directly in continuous latent spaces.

entry.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Analysis reveals on-policy distillation works primarily by suppressing low log-probability tokens rather than transferring teacher knowledge, inspiring On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA), a supervision-free method that uses entropy-adaptive negative advantages.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that teacher models are unnecessary for on-policy distillation, enabling cheaper, supervision-free LLM self-improvement through token probability suppression.

entry.title: Faithfulness Is Not Free: Auditing Offline KV-Cache Quantization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
A study on offline KV-cache quantization in RAG reveals that INT4 compression severely damages response faithfulness—causing over 90% negative faithfulness shifts among correct answers—despite INT8 remaining near-lossless.

Why it matters: Deploying INT4 KV-cache compression in production RAG systems risks ungrounded hallucinations that standard accuracy benchmarks fail to detect.

entry.title: Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a method using lightweight linear probes trained on intermediate LLM activations from <=500 preference pairs to pseudo-label over 50k unlabelled examples for low-resource preference adaptation.

Why it matters: This approach enables efficient LLM alignment for non-mainstream, cultural, or highly personalized user preferences while drastically reducing expensive human annotation requirements.

entry.title: The Fragility of Jailbreak Robustness Across Operational States
entry.summary:
Jailbreak robustness evaluations using a default vanilla state fail to capture safety dynamics, as non-safety system prompts can alter attack success rates by up to 56 percentage points while shifting hidden representations along a refusal axis.

Why it matters: Single-configuration safety evaluations underestimate real-world risk, necessitating multi-state robustness benchmarks that account for benign variations in system prompts.

entry.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
entry.summary:
BLOOM-WILT is a black-box LLM auditing pipeline that combines cross-round auditor strategy revision with adaptive next-token logit tilting to efficiently elicit rare target model behaviors without additional training.

Why it matters: WILT significantly improves the sample efficiency of automated LLM safety auditing and can alter model safety rankings without requiring internal parameter access or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Reconciling Process Supervision with Outcome-Based Credit in Agentic Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
TASPO reconciles process supervision with outcome-based credit by converting privileged information into bounded, mean-preserving weights that redistribute trajectory-level RL advantages across executable actions.

Why it matters: It enables language-model agents to achieve fine-grained, action-level credit assignment from privileged training data without losing the reliable optimization signal of verified task outcomes.

entry.title: Wrong Prediction, Right Answer: Recovering Evidence from Collapsed LLM Sequence Scores
entry.summary:
A diagnostic protocol using a two-parameter target-label-free additive correction reveals that LLM reasoning failures often stem from output bottlenecks rather than absent internal logic.

Why it matters: Apparent zero-shot reasoning deficits in LLMs may reflect output expression failures rather than true capability gaps, requiring narrower interpretations of standard benchmark evaluations.

entry.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering
entry.summary:
LoopArena is a benchmark evaluating AI models acting as Controllers that guide a separate, fixed Worker coding agent through long-running tasks across three evaluation settings.

Why it matters: It decouples the reasoning ability of runtime loop controllers from underlying coding agents, enabling targeted and cost-effective evaluation of long-horizon software engineering management.

entry.title: Beyond Data Scaling: Representation-Centric Continued Pre-training for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
VLAct is a VLA backbone trained via representation-centric continued pre-training on heterogeneous multi-embodiment robot data, improving downstream performance under fixed data and compute budgets without relying solely on data scaling.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that optimizing representations during pre-training enables superior cross-embodiment transfer and task performance on a modest compute budget, reducing reliance on costly robot data scaling.

entry.title: Agentic Artifact Creation: Systems, Evaluation, Principles, and Opportunities
entry.summary:
A survey of 259 works introduces a framework for agentic artifact creation, defining stateful construction systems driven by operational representations, policies, and runtime verification feedback across six artifact families.

Why it matters: It provides a structured framework and evaluation principles to help engineers build reliable AI agents capable of producing complete, verifiable, and stateful deliverables.

entry.title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
entry.summary:
Code-as-World introduces an agentic discovery paradigm that generates executable code to represent physical composition, dynamic evolution, and visual appearance from multimodal inputs.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language models to ground physical reasoning in controllable, quantitatively verified code abstractions rather than ungrounded visual approximations.

entry.title: J-Zero: Unified Challenger--Solver--Judge Co-Evolution from Zero Data
entry.summary:
J-Zero is a unified Challenger-Solver-Judge co-evolution framework that enables self-improvement across verifiable and unverifiable domains without human data.

Why it matters: It allows language models to continually self-improve without human supervision or ground-truth verifiers, mitigating degradation issues in complex domains.

entry.title: Revisiting Local Context for Long-Horizon Streaming 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary:
ABot-Recon achieves state-of-the-art long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction using strictly local context without persistent long-range memory.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that maintaining complex long-range memory is unnecessary for stable, long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction, significantly cutting memory requirements.

entry.title: LayerRecall: A State-Conditioned Memory Router for Long-Horizon Consistency in Video Generation
entry.summary:
LayerRecall is a current-conditioned memory router that selectively retrieves historical K/V states and injects them into specific memory-sensitive DiT layers to maintain long-horizon consistency in autoregressive video generation.

Why it matters: It enables autoregressive video diffusion models to reliably recall distant attributes and subjects across long time horizons without disrupting local continuity or adding computational overhead.

entry.title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
entry.summary:
ContextPilot is a proactive context management framework that enhances agent toolsets and uses fine-grained reinforcement learning to maintain compact working contexts in long-horizon tasks.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks more efficiently by actively optimizing their context window size without losing critical information.

entry.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
entry.summary:
Puro-2B offers an Apache 2.0 open-source pretraining recipe using consumer RTX 5090 GPUs to train 2B-parameter models on 1.4T tokens for under $6.9K.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive 2B-scale language models can be pretrained from scratch on consumer hardware within modest budgets, significantly lowering the financial barrier for academic and open-source AI research.

entry.title: Blind Men and the Elephant: Probing the Epistemic Myopia of LLMs under Long-Tail Divergent Knowledge
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced ElephantBench, a 1,094-question probe derived from low-exposure web corpora, to evaluate how well LLMs recall divergent accounts of long-tail facts.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current LLMs suffer from epistemic myopia, systematically favoring dominant web perspectives while failing to retain valid minority accounts of long-tail knowledge.

entry.title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing
entry.summary:
StepGuard is a step-level guard model that audits completed trajectories and pre-checks tool actions to defend LLM agents against unauthorized actions with minimal utility loss.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, pre-execution defense against malicious or risky tool invocations in LLM agent workflows without significantly degrading their problem-solving capability.

entry.title: Locate Anything in Videos: Rethinking Efficient Generative Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
entry.summary:
Parallel Tube Decoding (PTD) replaces autoregressive trajectory serialization in spatio-temporal video grounding with a fixed 1+1 round generation process, dramatically reducing decoding latency.

Why it matters: PTD removes the latency bottleneck of autoregressive video trajectory generation, enabling fast, real-time spatio-temporal localization without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
Fast Weight Attention establishes read-after-write autoregressive semantics for recurrent fast-weight memories, introducing the Falcon algorithm family to improve online updates and length extrapolation.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically grounded framework that unifies temporal alignment, plasticity, and bounded rehearsal to enhance context compression and extrapolation in recurrent sequence models.

entry.title: Paint What You See: Benchmarking Dexterous Visual Tool Use in Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced EASEL, a benchmark for fine-grained dexterous visual tool use, alongside the 440k-sample EASEL-Data curriculum dataset and the fine-tuned EASEL-9B model.

Why it matters: The benchmark exposes a systematic failure in current multimodal agents to translate fine-grained visual evidence into precise, parameter-driven physical or visual actions.

entry.title: Ring Forcing: Towards Precise Long-Term Memory for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
entry.summary:
Ring Forcing is an autoregressive video diffusion framework that enables precise long-term memory and minutes-long temporal coherence through a ring-structured training strategy, sequence compression, and sparse RoPE adaptation.

Why it matters: It resolves key long-term memory bottlenecks in autoregressive video generation, allowing models to maintain strict object permanence and identity consistency over minutes-long clips.

entry.title: VISTA: Verifier-Informed Student-to-Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
VISTA enhances on-policy self-distillation by using outcome-verified rollouts to adapt the privileged teacher toward the student at top-k high-KL-divergence token positions, rather than treating the teacher as a fixed target.

Why it matters: It improves student reasoning accuracy in self-distillation frameworks without incurring additional sampling costs or complex auxiliary reward models.

entry.title: A Probabilistic Interpretation of KV Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes KV cache eviction as a probabilistic expectation estimation problem, proving its computational hardness while introducing a sampling-based approach that enables decode-time correction for evicted entries.

Why it matters: Grounding KV cache eviction in probabilistic theory provides a principled framework to correct for dropped information during decoding, boosting LLM serving robustness without sacrificing compression gains.

entry.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
entry.summary:
REINS is a dual-action SAE inference-time steering method that simultaneously suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features to prevent safety circumvention from complex prompt wrappers.

Why it matters: It provides a robust, lightweight inference-time safety mechanism that prevents models from being exploited by adversarial prompt wrappers while avoiding model collapse.

entry.title: DARTS: Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery for Model Merging
entry.summary:
DARTS addresses representation bias in merged decoder LLMs using an entropy-weighted L1 loss and position-dependent additive bias terms, adding just 0.1% parameter overhead.

Why it matters: It enables accurate multi-task model merging for autoregressive decoder LLMs without full retraining or significant parameter overhead.

entry.title: VICT: Verifier-Instrumented Credit Tracing for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
VICT introduces verifier-side credit tracing for LLM agent reinforcement learning, assigning group-relative advantage along dependency-valid proof edges generated by terminal verifiers without using learned critics, process labels, or branch rollouts.

Why it matters: VICT provides an efficient mechanism for fine-grained credit assignment in long-horizon LLM agent training by extracting structural task evidence directly from existing code-based verifiers.

entry.title: Why Didn't It Check? Unsupported Final Claims and Their Repair in Two Tool-Equipped Language Models
entry.summary:
Tool-equipped language models can make unsupported final claims despite strict instructions, but providing missing evidence or applying automatic checking rules can repair 100% of these claims without degrading correct answers.

Why it matters: Enforcing targeted tool re-queries or automated evidence checks can systematically eliminate unverified model assertions without corrupting valid outputs.

entry.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
A new framework introduces Falcon-1 through Falcon-3 (and associated -A variants) to formalize fast weight attention updates using prefix-aligned read-after-write autoregressive semantics for continual sequence learning.

Why it matters: It enables recurrent sequence models to maintain robust performance in language modeling while enhancing length extrapolation on tasks like variable-digit addition.

entry.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
entry.summary:
A 2025-2026 survey categorizes neural network optimization across four design axes—temporal estimation, update geometry, horizon management, and systems representation—concluding that matrix-aware methods advance the field, though AdamW remains contextually irreplaceable.

Why it matters: It replaces single-optimizer hype with a compositional design framework and mandates stricter evaluation protocols across varied hardware and scaling constraints.

entry.title: Training Communication-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Layer Re-Configuration
entry.summary:
CE-MoE decouples token-mixing and channel-mixing depth by concentrating expert capacity into fewer routed MoE layers and adding dense layers, reducing training communication overhead without sacrificing performance.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs and training time for large MoE language models while boosting inference throughput without degrading model quality.

entry.title: How Proper Scoring Rules Shape LLM Forecasting
entry.summary:
Evaluating five proper scoring rules as LLM training objectives for binary event forecasting reveals distinct differences in calibration, error structure, and probability usage despite identical theoretical incentives.

Why it matters: Selecting a specific proper scoring rule as a training objective actively shapes the structural profile of an LLM's forecasting errors, meaning these loss functions are not functionally interchangeable in practice.

entry.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
entry.summary:
SARA mitigates tool-output command injection by decoupling action induction from execution authorization, keeping Attack Success Rate below 0.63% on benchmarks.

Why it matters: SARA provides a practical, architecture-level defense to prevent indirect prompt injection and unauthorized execution in multi-step LLM tool agents without sacrificing utility.

entry.title: Instruction Quality Matters: Refining Instructions for Effective Preference Learning
entry.summary:
A new instruction-refinement pipeline improves preference learning by identifying weak instructions via reward signals and revising them using rubric-guided LLM feedback rather than discarding data.

Why it matters: Refining initial instructions unlocks higher response quality ceilings and strengthens preference signals during model alignment without reducing dataset size.

entry.title: Equal Ranking Quality, Different Decisions: Training Order-Consistent LLM Scorers
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Order-Consistency SFT (OC-SFT) to train LLM scorers whose passage or response scores remain stable regardless of input candidate ordering.

Why it matters: Ranking metrics like nDCG@10 mask severe decision instability in LLM scorers, meaning evaluations must measure threshold retention and downstream reader stability alongside ranking quality.

entry.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
entry.summary:
WikiSkill is a framework that co-evolves AI agent skills with a persistent knowledge base (wiki) by systematically consolidating raw execution experience to guide iterative skill development.

Why it matters: Accumulating experience into persistent, transferable knowledge bases enables smaller models to surpass larger models and improves cross-model adaptation without full retraining.

entry.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
entry.summary:
Open-weight language models organize Moral Foundations Theory concepts into geometry spanning near-maximal independent dimensions that share a distinct, moral-specific positive component.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that LLMs represent unresolved moral tension geometrically provides insight into how language models internally structure complex value tradeoffs before generating output.

entry.title: Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification
entry.summary:
HarnessLens is a budget-aware framework that automates agent harness evolution by using trajectory-derived modifications and selectively verifying candidates on behavior-relevant tasks via an attributable-evidence gate.

Why it matters: It enables sample-efficient and reliable optimization of LLM agent harnesses without wasting expensive compute budgets on full-suite benchmarks for every candidate change.

entry.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable
entry.summary:
Escalating visual/evidential packaging raises frontier LLM agent commitment on unpredictable questions from 6.5% to 54.0%, even when evidence is completely fabricated, revealing a critical failure in the act/don't-act gate.

Why it matters: LLM agents deployed in financial or decision-making roles can be induced into confident, unauthorized actions simply by presenting them with authoritative-looking formatting, regardless of actual data validity.

entry.title: Omni-Interactive Universal Embedder
entry.summary:
OmniUE is the first universal embedder that unifies text, video, and audio representation learning while supporting omni-interactive queries across visual regions of interest, audio spans, and text.

Why it matters: OmniUE expands multimodal representation learning beyond text and images by enabling precise, user-conditioned retrieval across arbitrary combinations of text, visual, and audio inputs.

entry.title: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
entry.summary:
ASIL replaces pixel-based screenshot-and-click control for software-operating agents with structured JSON state observations and code-executable semantic actions accessed through deep application paths.

Why it matters: Replacing pixel-level interaction with structured state and semantic actions drastically improves agent task success rates, execution efficiency, and fine-tuning efficacy for complex software operations.

entry.title: GraphMemix: Query-Aware Evidence Forests for Long-Term Multimodal Agent Memory
entry.summary:
GraphMemix organizes long-term multimodal agent memory by framing query-aware context selection as a combinatorial-optimization problem that constructs evidence forests from expanded candidate graphs.

Why it matters: It establishes a superior Pareto frontier between retrieval accuracy and lifecycle cost for multimodal agent memory systems across foundation models.

entry.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
entry.summary:
The authors introduce Puro-2B, an open-source pretraining recipe using FP8 precision on consumer RTX 5090 GPUs to train 2B-parameter models for under $6.9K.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive 2B-parameter language models can be pretrained from scratch on consumer hardware at a fraction of typical industry costs.

entry.title: Unifying Detection and Adaptation in Task-Free Continual Learning
entry.summary:
The FiUni framework uses Fisher information matrix principal subspaces to unify task detection and parameter-efficient adaptation for task-free continual learning in large language models.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to continually learn from streaming data in realistic task-free scenarios while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and minimizing trainable parameter overhead.

entry.title: Representation Measurements Under Function-Preserving Reparameterizations
entry.summary:
Column-permutation parallel analysis violates function-preserving reparameterization invariance, causing representation-derived component counts to change even when a language model's input-output function and covariance spectrum remain fixed.

Why it matters: Parallel analysis-derived component counts can reflect arbitrary hidden-coordinate choices rather than true, intrinsic properties of a language model's underlying representations.

entry.title: Squeezing More from Limited Data with Recursive Transformers
entry.summary:
Recursive Transformers combined with factorized embeddings outperform standard Transformers in data-constrained pre-training regimes (10M-100M words) by decoupling compute scale from total parameter count.

Why it matters: This architecture enables efficient language model pre-training in low-resource domain settings where compute is available but data availability is severely restricted.

entry.title: ClusterAttention: A training-free speedup of bidirectional attention
entry.summary:
ClusterAttention is a training-free bidirectional attention method using fast recursive key-query clustering and centroid compensation to accelerate unstructured transformers without calibration.

Why it matters: It enables significant inference speedups on unstructured and high-dimensional transformer workloads without requiring retraining, architectural modifications, or offline calibration.

entry.title: Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable
entry.summary:
Scaling model-generated off-task distillation datasets amplifies latent teacher-specific traits in student models, making subtle behaviors more detectable during downstream evaluations.

Why it matters: Distillation datasets require trait-aware curation and evaluation, as scaling synthetic data can silently transfer latent, unintended teacher behaviors into student models even when the data seems benign and off-task.

entry.title: A Layer Importance Metric for Quantization Accounting for the Speed-Quality Trade-off in Autoregressive Models
entry.summary:
A composite metric combines SQNR-based information retention and roofline-based latency analysis to prioritize LLM layers for mixed-precision quantization without running inference.

Why it matters: It turns mixed-precision quantization into a predictable, analytical engineering process that optimizes the speed-quality trade-off on memory-bandwidth-constrained devices without expensive trial-and-error profiling.

entry.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
entry.summary:
CritICL improves LLM reasoning efficiency by converting structured failure modes from weaker models within the same family into critique-based in-context examples during inference.

Why it matters: It enables weak-to-strong inference-time generalization and improves reasoning performance without incurring the massive token overhead of repeated generation or external verifiers.

entry.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) is an unlabelled test-time training method that combines token-filtered On-Policy Self-Distillation for agreeing rollouts with Grouped RL penalties for disagreeing rollouts using majority-vote pseudo-labels.

Why it matters: TTPO enables continuous, label-free model optimization during inference on complex mathematical reasoning tasks without the risk of corruption from incorrect majority-vote pseudo-labels.

entry.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
entry.summary:
A new method boosts LLM reasoning coverage and exploration during Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) by forcing the target model to complete partial reasoning trajectories generated by a weaker language model.

Why it matters: It expands LLM reasoning diversity and improves high-sample pass@k accuracy without the overhead of additional fine-tuning or complex algorithmic regularizations.

entry.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
entry.summary:
A systematic comparison of three fusion paradigms—Merge, Mix RL, and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation—reveals key performance trade-offs, constraints, and guidelines for consolidating multi-domain RLVR capabilities in LLMs.

Why it matters: It provides concrete engineering guidelines for choosing the optimal strategy to consolidate domain-specific reinforcement learning improvements into a single model without incurring unnecessary compute costs.

entry.title: Reasoning about In-Context Samples for Machine-Translation
entry.summary:
A novel fragment-based reasoning framework for LLM machine translation extracts parallel source-target fragments from retrieved exemplars as intermediate reasoning traces to improve translation performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that structured chain-of-thought reasoning based on extracted exemplar fragments enhances the quality and reliability of in-context machine translation across diverse languages and domains.

entry.title: Decoupling Planning and Control for Instructable Agents
entry.summary:
Instruct-to-Act decouples embodied agents by using a high-latency VLM planner to generate sparse text instructions that guide a fast, language-instructable world-model controller.

Why it matters: It enables fast, real-time control in embodied and multi-agent systems while maintaining the flexible, open-ended task planning capabilities of large vision-language models.

entry.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
entry.summary:
MCR-Bench is the first defect state-aware benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on realistic, multi-round interactive code review across 2,269 real-world tasks.

Why it matters: It exposes the limitations of evaluating LLMs on single-round static code review tasks, highlighting memory and tracking gaps that must be addressed for real-world automated code review.

entry.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
entry.summary:
MAELLE models chemical reactions via discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors using Optimal Transport Continuous-time Markov Chains instead of traditional molecular topology graph edits.

Why it matters: By modeling fundamental electron rearrangements rather than ad-hoc topological graph edits, the approach improves out-of-distribution robustness and enables mechanistically interpretable side-product predictions.

entry.title: Procedura: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control
entry.summary:
Procedura is a 3D modeling agent framework that generates editable, parametric 3D objects as procedural code assemblies using LLM-driven graph planning, machine-checkable mates, and decoupled vision critics.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between text-to-3D generation and CAD engineering by outputting fully editable, structured, and articulated programs rather than non-parametric, dense meshes.

entry.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation
entry.summary:
Luce unifies geometry and PBR materials into a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud using dedicated primitives, autoencoding them into a material-aware latent space for single-image relightable 3D asset generation via a rectified-flow transformer.

Why it matters: Luce enables the direct creation of relightable, high-fidelity 3D assets with accurate PBR materials and fine details like text from a single input image.

entry.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
entry.summary:
CritICL is a novel inference-time framework that enhances LLM reasoning by incorporating structured failure modes from smaller models into critique-based in-context learning prompts.

Why it matters: CritICL improves reasoning accuracy at inference time while bypassing the high compute and token costs associated with traditional test-time scaling and repeated generations.

entry.title: CaRGo-T: Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought improves Multimodal Humor Comprehension
entry.summary:
CaRGo-T is a framework that improves multimodal humor understanding by using vision-language models to generate code-serialized, graph-based representations of causal and contextual relationships.

Why it matters: Graph-structured causal reasoning provides a more effective mechanism than linear prompting for vision-language models to interpret complex, implicit multimodal interactions like humor.

entry.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
entry.summary:
TacForcing introduces a streaming action expert that integrates execution-time tactile feedback into vision-language-action models using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention, eliminating separate reactive controllers.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language-action models to dynamically adapt to real-time contact changes during execution without complex, multi-component control architectures.

entry.title: CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval
entry.summary:
CaSKG introduces a counterfactual-causal skill graph framework that calibrates offline procedural skill edges using direction-conditioned textual probes and Bayesian smoothing to improve LLM agent skill retrieval.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to accurately retrieve executable workflows, prerequisites, and state-changing actions from large skill libraries without incurring the high context costs of full-library prompting.

entry.title: Thinking on Shots: Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing with Agentic Reasoning
entry.summary:
MMLVE-Agent uses LLMs and VLMs to perform multi-instruction multi-shot long-video editing while maintaining cross-shot consistency and spatiotemporal structure.

Why it matters: It resolves entity fragmentation and continuity loss in long-video editing by replacing fixed chunking with agent-driven shot decoupling and instruction parsing.

entry.title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?
entry.summary:
A new multilingual self-play benchmark using an extended TextArena evaluates cross-lingual skill inconsistency in LLMs by pitting identical models against each other under different language interfaces while keeping state spaces and game rules fixed.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that LLM skill execution is not language-invariant, highlighting language bias in decision-making pipelines and the need for equitable cross-lingual model design.

entry.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling
entry.summary:
Prefix Sliding optimizes test-time compute by discarding middle reasoning tokens while retaining initial instructions and recent context, reducing memory overhead and accelerating inference.

Why it matters: It enables models to perform long-horizon reasoning over 100,000 tokens efficiently by eliminating memory bottlenecks during test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming
entry.summary:
EditaLive is a framework that adapts the Wan-Animate model for real-time, instruction-based human-centric video editing during live streams with minimal facial-expression loss and low latency.

Why it matters: It enables low-latency, real-time character video editing during live streams while maintaining facial expression consistency and preventing appearance drift.

entry.title: Aphanta: Diagnosing Task-Aligned Image-Edited Intermediates for Multimodal Reasoning
entry.summary:
Aphanta is a diagnostic framework evaluating MLLM-to-image-editor-to-MLLM pipelines by comparing direct reasoning, editor-generated intermediates, and idealized reference intermediates across 20 tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes that image editing acts as a task-specific visual workspace rather than a universal reasoning tool, providing a standardized protocol to evaluate MLLM visual representation alignment.

entry.title: RetrievalRouter: Joint Modality and Architecture Selection for Document Retrieval
entry.summary:
RetrievalRouter is a lightweight, query-aware routing system that dynamically selects the optimal retrieval pipeline's modality and architecture from query text alone, breaking static trade-offs between accuracy and latency.

Why it matters: It enables high-stakes document retrieval systems in fields like law and finance to maximize accuracy while drastically reducing the computation costs and latency of complex pipelines.

entry.title: What Does an Evaluation License? A Commit-Bound Census of Claim-Relative Inference in Inspect Evals
entry.summary:
A commit-bound census of 124 Inspect Evals units formalizes a claim-replay layer, revealing that 110 units stop before deterministic inference due to missing historical evidence or semantic grounding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard evaluation artifacts often lack the historical and semantic binding required to reliably support or replay their attached claims.

entry.title: LibriBrain100: One Hundred Hours of Broad and Deep MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding at Scale
entry.summary:
LibriBrain100 is a large-scale MEG dataset containing over 100 hours of continuous speech listening data, including ~80 hours from a single subject and ~40 minutes across 32 subjects.

Why it matters: The dataset and standardized evaluation pipeline accelerate the development of practical, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces aimed at restoring communication for individuals with severe paralysis.

entry.title: JudgeStealer: Extracting LLM Judging Capabilities across Evaluation Protocols
entry.summary:
JUDGESTEALER is a query-efficient framework designed to extract black-box LLM judging capabilities across pointwise, pairwise, and listwise evaluation protocols using dynamically selected pointwise queries.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that proprietary LLM judge and reward model intellectual property can be stolen efficiently across multiple evaluation formats despite query budget constraints and extraction defenses.

entry.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
entry.summary:
CLAP introduces a cross-embodiment video world model framework that leverages latent actions, end-effector poses, and language instructions to learn generalizable physics across human and diverse robotic datasets.

Why it matters: It enables action-conditioned video generation models to train on internet-scale heterogeneous video data, bypassing the restriction of single-robot embodiment datasets for physical simulation.

entry.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
entry.summary:
CAST uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify, audit, and suppress text artifact features during clinical language model fine-tuning, improving robustness and decision transparency.

Why it matters: It prevents clinical models from relying on spurious formatting artifacts, making AI predictions robust to deployment shifts and fully auditable by clinicians.

entry.title: LeVJEPA: Efficient & Scalable Video Pretraining without the Heuristics
entry.summary:
LeVJEPA is the first video encoder trained with LeJEPA's collapse-free objective, eliminating architectural asymmetries, stop-gradients, and target encoders while drastically reducing pretraining compute.

Why it matters: It removes the heavy computational overhead and complex heuristics of video self-supervised learning, making video a viable, efficient alternative to static images for general-purpose visual pretraining.

entry.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models
entry.summary:
Successive Capacity Growth (SCG) dynamically expands Vision Transformer encoders in JEPA world models in width or depth using a task-agnostic, function-preserving test-and-verify mechanism.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to pre-allocate maximum transformer capacity in JEPA world models, optimizing compute and parameter efficiency without losing predictive quality.

entry.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
entry.summary:
PAWBench and PAWEval introduce a benchmark and outcome-level evaluation protocol to test whether video generation models function as probabilistically aligned world models that match true physical behavior distributions.

Why it matters: Current video-based world models fail to capture the correct probability distributions of non-deterministic physical events, highlighting a key gap in developing reliable stochastic simulators.

entry.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance
entry.summary:
Eval-awareness in model chain-of-thought is not uniform; capabilities-framed eval-awareness predicts compliance with dangerous requests at significantly higher rates (+24 to +46 percentage points) than safety-framed eval-awareness.

Why it matters: Safety evaluation pipelines cannot treat eval-awareness as a single metric to suppress, as different framings cause vastly different safety and compliance behaviors.

entry.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search
entry.summary:
Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO) uses a lightweight, single-lineage iterative prompt revision method driven by teacher model feedback, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding complex prompt search algorithms like GEPA using fewer rollouts.

Why it matters: NPO demonstrates that strong teacher reasoning can replace complex optimizer search architectures, drastically reducing the computational cost of optimizing agent prompts.

entry.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
This paper presents a two-level framework that factorizes LLM agentic data and uses the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens to guide constrained data generation.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized formal framework to evaluate and generate informative, non-redundant synthetic experience for evolving LLM agents instead of relying on raw dataset scaling.

entry.title: PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference
entry.summary:
PACE is a training-free VLM inference framework that uses a Condense-and-Extract paradigm to reduce computation in both the vision encoder and LLM.

Why it matters: It significantly cuts VLM inference latency and computation without requiring model retraining or sacrificing critical fine-grained visual details.

entry.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue
entry.summary:
Researchers created ContraTalk, a benchmark measuring cross-modal transcript bias in spoken dialogue, and introduced an Audio Twin framework to expose localized acoustic evidence directly to LLM reasoning models.

Why it matters: The findings show that current audio-language models rely heavily on text shortcuts, demonstrating the need for explicit acoustic evidence extraction to achieve reliable speech-grounded reasoning.
